steps.title: Confirm metabolic alkalosis
steps.body: Elevated pH and bicarbonate. Assess volume status, blood pressure, and medications (diuretics, vomiting).
steps.tip: Vomiting and loop/thiazide diuretics are the most common causes.

steps.title: Check urine chloride
steps.body: Urine Cl− <20 mEq/L suggests chloride-responsive (saline-responsive) alkalosis from volume depletion or GI losses.
steps.tip: Urine Cl− >20 = chloride-resistant — think mineralocorticoid excess.

steps.title: Volume repletion
steps.body: Give isotonic saline to restore extracellular volume. Kidney excretes bicarbonate once chloride and volume are restored.
steps.tip: Avoid overcorrection in heart failure — use cautious diuresis strategy.

steps.title: Chloride-resistant causes
steps.body: If urine Cl− >20: primary hyperaldosteronism, Cushing, licorice, severe hypokalemia, or current diuretic use.
steps.tip: Severe hypokalemia perpetuates alkalosis — correct K+.

steps.title: Adjunct therapy
steps.body: Acetazolamide increases bicarbonate excretion. HCl infusion reserved for severe refractory alkalosis in ICU settings.
steps.tip: Treat the underlying mineralocorticoid excess when chloride-resistant.
